findings.issue: Carried over from the first review, unchanged. Maya's `$` budget can be found, but 'if it's pricey' is relative, so the player has to work out that one dollar sign counts as not pricey. The trip fund callback, the iced tea line, a downtown range of only `$`/`$$`, and Cardamom House's 'treat-yourself lunch' review mean a careful player still gets there. It's still the softest clue in the level.
findings.suggested_fix: Point at the cheapest end without naming a tier, e.g. 'and the trip fund is watching. cheapest curry in town or i'm eating crackers at my desk'.

findings.issue: Carried over, unchanged. 'a real main' is the signature phrase of the level_16 'Mina speaks up' beat ('could we go somewhere I can order a real main this time?'). Using it twice here, through Liam and in Mina's perfect reaction, takes a little away from that later payoff.
findings.suggested_fix: Liam: 'ok ok. but mina gets an actual curry this time. no plate of fries'; Mina's perfect line: 'i had a whole curry of my own, and liam didn't have to watch me eat a side. thank you :)'.

findings.issue: Partly fixed. Maya's new line no longer copies level_05 word for word, and 'leaving this restaurant' is a nice twist on her catchphrase. But the beat is the same: Maya walks out and takes Mina with her (level_05: 'taking mina with me'). Mina's line wasn't changed and is still the level_03/level_05 template: 'oh. every [dish] here has meat... it's okay, i'll just have some [water/rice]'.
findings.suggested_fix: Mina: 'oh. it's all lamb and chicken. the rice is nice though, honestly'. Maya could get a different dramatic beat, e.g. 'this is OUTRAGEOUS! i'm leaving this restaurant. we are NOT doing fries 2.0'.

findings.issue: Liam's edited reply opens with 'ok ok.', and so does his line six bubbles later ('ok ok. but mina orders a real main'). Two identical openers this close together read like a tic, not a voice. The new line itself ('in, eat, out. my stomach and i are ready') is short and food-first, so it fits his voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the opener in script[5]: 'in, eat, out. my stomach and i are ready'. Or change script[11] to 'fine. but mina gets...'.

findings.issue: The edit fixes the earlier copy of level_05 ('thank you both' is gone, and the leading '...' is her usual hesitation, so it's fine). It's soft, offhand and confirmable from reviews, so it fits clue rule 6. But the line now says 'okay' twice ('...okay.' and 'if that's okay'), which reads a bit clumsy.
findings.suggested_fix: '...okay. somewhere with a few curries i can actually order would be really nice, if you don't mind'.

findings.issue: The edited review clearly proves Indigo Arch isn't a quick lunch: the curry still hadn't arrived when the reviewer gave up, and the courses come one at a time. Together with review 2's 'long Saturday dinner', no careful player would mistake it for quick. Now 'Very slow paced.' states the fact outright. The map-seeder brief asks implied-level reviews to hint through experience, and the experience before it already makes the point.
findings.suggested_fix: Cut the last sentence, or swap it for an experience: '...Courses taste lovely but come out one at a time. I was back at my desk well after one.'

summary: Still a fair, warm implied level, and Gabriella's edits mostly help. quick_bite is now easier to find: 'gonna be another quick lunch' plus Liam's 'in, eat, out' is close to stated, which matches level_03's precedent for a soft vibe in an implied level, while the hard vegetarian clue stays properly implied through the two callbacks and Mina's soft acceptance. Indigo Arch's review proves slowness without doubt. All six findings are suggestions: earlier suggestions 5 and 6 are fixed apart from small wording points, 3 is only partly fixed (Mina's fail line and Maya's 'take Mina with me' beat still echo level_05), and 1 and 2 are unchanged.
